title: Waiting long and holding tight
meaning: Postponed pleasure can become too precious when waiting makes you hold onto an evening after your wishes have changed.
text: The longer pleasure is postponed, the more significance it can acquire. The Empress in the physical position of Svadhisthana helps you create enjoyment: choosing delicious things, imagining a lovely setting and making something together. The Hanged Man in energy keeps desire waiting, prompting another look at the conditions instead of a beginning. The Devil in emotions shows how difficult it can then feel to release a rare pleasure. The evening must finally make up for every postponement, and free enjoyment risks becoming an obligation to obtain as much from it as possible.

Imagine you have long intended to make ice cream at home. An hour finally becomes available: you choose toppings and taste the first spoonfuls. **A long wait does not oblige pleasure to outlast your desire.** You can enjoy one successful serving and leave the rest for tomorrow. The hour retains its value through shared flavour and conversation, even if your whole imagined celebration does not fit the available time.

The difficulty lies in charging leisure for how long you waited. Stopping feels awkward, changing the idea disappointing, and differing moods can seem to devalue the effort. You hold onto the preparations more tightly than each other’s actual enjoyment. The waiting has ended, yet its conditions still govern the evening. A wish can be partly fulfilled and still bring the two of you real pleasure.
